questions.knowledge_point: Describing Non-Rectangular Sets Using Set-Builder Notation
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044982/assets/5c4ffbb64a754df9a6100fda3fd6eaf4a68f28ac59de4dfb716c2c8b1f2847ab.png)

Use set builder notation to describe the shaded region given in the diagram above:

$$
{(x,y)\in {{field-1}}\,:\,y\,{{field-2}}\,{x}^{2}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *below* the curve $y={x}^{2}.$

Therefore, a point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following condition is satisfied:

$$
y<{x}^{2}
$$

We must also include the curve $y={x}^{2}$ since the boundary is included in the set (the curve is solid). So, we change the inequality symbol above as follows:

$$
y\le {x}^{2}
$$

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,y\le {x}^{2}}.
$$

Describe the shaded region shown above using set-builder notation.

$$
{(x,y)\in {{field-1}}\,:\,-x\,{{field-2}}\,y\,{{field-3}}\,2}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *above* the line $y=-x$ and *below* the line $y=2.$

A point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following conditions are satisfied:

$$
y>-x,\,y<2.
$$

Combining this into a single condition, we have

$$
-x<y<2.
$$

We must also include the line $y=-x$ since the boundary is included in the set (the curve is solid). So, we change the corresponding inequality symbol above as follows:

$$
-x\le y<2
$$

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,-x\le y<2}.
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Describing Non-Rectangular Sets Using Set-Builder Notation
questions.worked_solution:
The equation of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ is given by

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

 

Here, the elliptical boundary of our region has horizontal radius $a=2$ and vertical radius $b=3.$ Therefore, the equation of the ellipse is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{x}^{2}}{4}+\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1,\end{aligned}
$$

which we can write as

$$
9{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}=36.
$$

We're interested in describing all points that lie *inside* the ellipse. So, let's pick any point inside the region, say, $(0,0).$ Substituting its coordinates into the equation of the boundary, we obtain

$$
9(0)^{2}+4(0)^{2}\,<\,36.
$$

As a result, the points $P(x,y)$ in our region are any real numbers that satisfy the condition

$$
9{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}<36.
$$

We must also include the curve $9{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}=36$ since the boundary is included in the set (the curve is solid). So, we change the inequality symbol above as follows:

$$
9{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}\le 36.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,9{x}^{2}+4{y}^{2}\le 36}.
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The points in our set include all those that lie *above* the line $y=2.$

Therefore, a point $P(x,y)$ lies *inside* the shaded region if the following condition is satisfied:

$$
y>2
$$

Since the boundary is *not* included in the set (the curve is *not* solid),  no further action must be taken, so we have

$$
y>2.
$$

Moreover, since we're considering *every* real value in this region, $x\in R,y\in R,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in R\times R={R}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as

$$
{(x,y)\in {R}^{2}\,:\,y>2}.
$$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14044982/assets/f54c771d1b7045bbaa301c9d595a45dc64fbdfc6b1c83c152fb6fc892373ea06.png)

Describe the shaded region shown above using set-builder notation.

$$
{(x,y)\in {{field-1}}\,:\,y\,{{field-2}}\,-1}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since all points $P(x,y)$ in our set lie at integer values of $x$ and $y,$ we have $x\in Z,y\in Z,$ and therefore 

$$
(x,y)\in Z\times Z={Z}^{2}.
$$

The points in our set include all those that lie *above* the line $y=-1.$ For those points, the following condition is satisfied:

$$
y>-1
$$

Also, notice that some points in our set lie *on* the line. We include these points by changing the inequality symbol above as follows:

$$
y\ge -1
$$

Therefore, we can write the set as follows:

$$
{(x,y)\in {Z}^{2}\,:\,y\ge -1}
$$
